questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$18\,000$ at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$) is repaid with $\$350$ per month.
How many whole monthly repayments are required to pay off the loan?

options.why: Rounded down to 59, leaving an unpaid balance.
Reported a fractional number of repayments instead of a whole number.
Used the annual rate with the monthly $n$.

questions.question_text:
A borrower owes $\$30\,000$ on a line of credit charging $12\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.01$).
If repayments are set to $\$280$ per month, what will happen to the loan?

options.text: The loan will never be repaid because the monthly repayment is less than the monthly interest charge of $\$300$.
The loan will be repaid in $108$ months.
options.why: Calculated term ignoring that interest exceeds repayments.

options.text: The loan balance will remain constant at $\$30\,000$.
options.why: Assumed the repayment matches the interest exactly.

options.text: The loan will be repaid in $120$ months with a larger final payment.
options.why: Assumed any regular payment eventually pays off the principal.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Monthly interest}=30\,000\times0.01=\$300$
Since the $\$280$ repayment is less than the $\$300$ interest, the debt grows each month and the loan is never repaid.

If repayments are increased to $\$800$ per month, how many months earlier is the loan paid off?

options.why: Reported the new loan term instead of the time saved.

questions.question_text:

What is the value of $(1.0075)^{n}$ when $A_{n}=0$?

options.why: Divided repayment by principal instead of solving the geometric series equation.

questions.question_text: When a loan requires $47.3$ theoretical monthly repayments of $\$500$, how should the final payment on month $48$ be handled?

options.text: The borrower makes 47 full repayments of $\$500$ and a 48th smaller payment covering the remaining compounded balance.

options.why: Multiplied the fractional part directly by the payment amount without compounding the remaining balance.

options.text: The borrower makes 47 full payments and the remaining balance is forgiven.
options.why: Mistakenly assumes remaining debt is cancelled after integer periods.

options.text: The borrower must make 48 full payments of $\$500$.
options.why: Overpays the loan by making a full final repayment.

questions.solution_text:
A fractional result of $47.3$ periods means $47$ regular payments are made.
The remaining unpaid balance compounds for one more month and is cleared by a 48th smaller payment.

questions.question_text: For a loan of $\$PV$ at periodic rate $r$ with repayment $M$, what condition ensures the logarithm in $n=\dfrac{\log\left(\frac{M}{M-PV\,r}\right)}{\log(1+r)}$ is defined with $n>0$?

options.why: Confused periodic interest with simple linear principal division.
Reversed the inequality, which results in a negative argument in the logarithm.
Demanded full principal repayment in a single period.

questions.solution_text:
For $\dfrac{M}{M-PV\,r}>1$, the denominator must be positive and strictly less than the numerator.
This requires $M-PV\,r>0\implies M>PV\times r$, meaning the payment exceeds periodic interest.
